useCases.title: Seal: independent review of AI decision evidence
useCases.summary: A bank declines a loan application. Six months later, the customer's solicitor asks why. The only record is a log written by the organisation under review. Seal separates the evidence across three independent parties: Seal signs the decision receipt, Yivi issues the reviewer's credential, and the reviewer signs the verdict. No single party controls the complete evidence path. A reviewer opens a docket with one fixed question, set before the evidence is opened so it cannot be adjusted to fit the answer, verifies the receipt against Seal's published key, and records one of three verdicts: accepted, declined, or not enough to answer. A reviewer outside Aqta, holding a credential we did not issue, has completed the prototype flow and signed a verdict. Walk it at review.aqta.ai or tamper with a receipt at app.aqta.ai/demo. What it establishes: Seal signed the stated record; signed fields have not changed; a reviewer signed a verdict on a fixed question. What it does not establish: that the record matches the computation that ran, or that every decision was recorded. We would rather be checked than believed. Signing is production; this review flow is a prototype and the page says so.
useCases.userJourney:
1. Seal signs an AI decision as it is made. The receipt is offline-verifiable against Seal's published Ed25519 key
2. A reviewer opens a docket: one fixed question, set before the evidence is opened so it cannot be adjusted to fit the answer, with the receipt attached. The question is hashed into what will be signed
3. The reviewer verifies the receipt in their own browser against the published key, then chooses one of three verdicts: accept, decline, or not enough to answer
4. The page requests an IRMA signature session. The reviewer's Yivi wallet shows the exact binding text: receipt hash, question hash, decision, timestamp
5. The reviewer signs by disclosing a verified email credential from their wallet. No account is created with the relying party
6. The relying party verifies that attribute-based signature with irmago, the open-source IRMA library, the moment anchored by the Yivi timestamp service
7. The pack exports receipt, credential presentation and countersignature. Each verifies without contacting Aqta: the receipt with the open-source verifiers on npm and PyPI, the signature with irmago, since no browser Idemix verifier exists
